content:
sara (Support): Escalation: customer AcmeCorp reported intermittent invalid JSON coming back when using structured_output mode. High severity customer impact.
maya (Customer Success): Ticket #AC-4721 - customer says production started failing ~2026-02-22 14:02 UTC, multiple requests. Link: https://acme.support/AC-4721
oncall-bot: ALERT json_parse_failure_rate > 5% in prod/us-east-1 for route /v1/generate. Alert id: alert-8923
sara (Support): Example request id: req_hQ2n9Z. Customer provided failing response below.
liam (ML Eng): Please paste failing response and the prompt if possible.
sara (Support): here's the curl they used:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-14b","structured_output":{"mode":"json","schema_version":"v2"},"input":"Generate invoice items for order #98431"}'
```

sara (Support): Response (as received):
```
{"items":[{"sku":"ABC-1","qty":2},],"total":39.98}
```

tom (SRE): That trailing comma in the array will break strict JSON parsers. Need to check where it was emitted (model vs postprocessor).
liam (ML Eng): Agreed. Does this happen for other customers or only AcmeCorp?
nick (DataOps): Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/struct-output shows a spike in parse errors starting 2026-02-21 23:50 UTC; p50 latency slightly up. Query: sum by(model_variant,route) (increase(json_parse_failure_total[1h]))
aisha (Product): We rolled out prompt template change tied to schema v2 last week. Could be prompt causing dangling punctuation.
maya (Customer Success): Customer says it affects ~2% of calls but blocks their ingestion pipeline because they enforce strict JSON.
liam (ML Eng): Repro steps requested: set model to redwood-14b and structured_output schema_version v2, send sample inputs with list-building instructions. I'll add an integration test.
sara (Support): Customer gave an additional failing snippet where a string contained unescaped newlines causing JSON error.
liam (ML Eng): Two hypotheses: model hallucinating a literal trailing comma, or postprocessor truncation that leaves a trailing token. Need full raw token-level output and model_variant (e.g., redwood-14b-qat-1).
sara (Support): internal note: please capture X-Request-ID and traceparent headers for traces.

tom (SRE): Actionable telemetry we need now:
- Add tag json_schema_version to json_parse_failure metric
- Log structured field parse_error=true, parser_error_detail (first 256 chars) but redact PII
- Ensure traces include span for structured-output postprocess
- Retain raw_model_output in S3 for 7 days for failed parses (access controlled)

liam (ML Eng): Quick mitigation: enable lenient postprocessor that strips trailing commas and attempts a second parse, but log both versions and set metric parse_repair_count.
aisha (Product): Must be opt-in per-customer until we verify no silent data corruption. Add product flag feature.switch.structured_output.lenient_repair

sara (Support): For AcmeCorp, can we enable lenient_repair behind their account toggle? They approved temporary opt-in.

tom (SRE): I'll provision a canary toggle for AcmeCorp and wire the repair flow. ETA 2h. Will also add dashboard panel for repaired vs failed.

nick (DataOps): Dashboard queries to add:
- json_parse_failure_rate by schema_version and model_variant
- percent_repaired = repaired_count / (repaired_count + failed_count)
- p99 latency for structured_output route

liam (ML Eng): I'll push a unit test that asserts no trailing commas for list outputs and add fuzzing for edge cases (embedded newlines, unescaped quotes).
maya (Customer Success): Customer asks for repro steps to run locally. Can we give them a minimal curl that toggles lenient_repair? e.g., add header `X-Structured-Repair: true`.
sara (Support): I'll send the customer the temporary toggle and ask for logs with X-Request-ID. Also flag billing team if they want compensation.

aisha (Product): Longer term: consider adding schema version negotiation and a machine-readable parse status in the API response so clients can programmatically fallback.

sara (Support): Summary/owners:
- tom (SRE): enable per-customer lenient repair, add metrics/dashboards (2h)
- liam (ML Eng): repro tests + fuzzing + postprocessor audit (EOD)
- nick (DataOps): add dashboard panels + grafana alerts (4h)
- maya (Customer Success): coordinate with AcmeCorp and provide temporary toggle (ASAP)
- aisha (Product): product flag and api response design (next sprint)

sara (Support): Marking P1 for customer ingestion pipelines. Will update thread when canary is live. :white_check_mark:

:thumbsup: reactions from team
